name: Japanese
era: Nara/Heian period - Edo period (Yasui Santetsu / Shibukawa Harumi, Tenmon Seisho)
description: Japan's adaptation of the Chinese star system as shown on the Edo-era Yasui (Shibukawa Harumi) star map, with Japanese readings, the 28 shuku with their native star names, and 61 asterisms (J01-J61) unique to Japan named for the Ritsuryo court offices.

figures.name: Ministry of Central Affairs
figures.group: Japanese additions (Tenmon Kyoto)
figures.story: This ministry was the highest administrative body in the ancient Japanese government, responsible for the Imperial family's affairs and the administration of the court.

figures.name: Ministry of Ceremonies
figures.group: Japanese additions (Tenmon Kyoto)
figures.story: Responsible for the management of the court rank system, personnel records, and the oversight of rites and ceremonies held within the imperial palace.

figures.name: Ministry of Civil Administration
figures.group: Japanese additions (Tenmon Kyoto)
figures.story: In charge of the administration of court rituals, the management of temples and shrines, and the oversight of the Buddhist clergy.

figures.name: Ministry of Popular Affairs
figures.group: Japanese additions (Tenmon Kyoto)
figures.story: Managed the census, taxes, civil engineering projects, and the general welfare of the common populace under the Ritsuryō system.

figures.name: Ministry of Military Affairs
figures.group: Japanese additions (Tenmon Kyoto)
figures.story: Overseeing the defense and military structure of the nation, including the mobilization of soldiers and the management of military records.

figures.name: Ministry of Justice
figures.group: Japanese additions (Tenmon Kyoto)
figures.story: Responsible for the administration of laws, the conduct of trials, and the maintenance of order and security within the capital.

figures.name: Ministry of Finance
figures.group: Japanese additions (Tenmon Kyoto)
figures.story: Managed the national treasury, including taxation, currency, and the distribution of salaries to government officials.

figures.name: Ministry of the Imperial Household
figures.group: Japanese additions (Tenmon Kyoto)
figures.story: Dedicated to the management of the private affairs of the Imperial family, including the maintenance of the palace grounds and services for the Emperor.

figures.name: Tutor to the Crown Prince
figures.group: Japanese additions (Tenmon Kyoto)
figures.story: Representing the figures responsible for the education, guidance, and character development of the next Emperor.

figures.name: Lady of the Bedchamber
figures.group: Japanese additions (Tenmon Kyoto)
figures.story: A high-ranking lady in waiting who served the Emperor within the Inner Palace and held significant political influence.

figures.name: Palace Table Office
figures.group: Japanese additions (Tenmon Kyoto)
figures.story: Responsible for the preparation and management of food and banquet services for the court and official functions.

figures.name: Inner Palace Table Office
figures.group: Japanese additions (Tenmon Kyoto)
figures.story: Focusing specifically on the preparation of meals served directly to the Emperor and the Empress within the private residential quarters.

figures.name: Department of Divinities
figures.group: Japanese additions (Tenmon Kyoto)
figures.story: A government agency that operated outside the standard civil ministries, dedicated to the administration of Shinto rites and ancestral worship.

figures.name: Celestial Sail
figures.group: Japanese additions (Tenmon Kyoto)
figures.story: Symbolizing the movement and navigation of heavenly bodies across the sky, often associated with the imperial transition.

figures.name: Major Captain
figures.group: Japanese additions (Tenmon Kyoto)
figures.story: Refers to a high-ranking military officer who commanded the Imperial Guards and held significant influence in the imperial court.

figures.name: Middle Captain
figures.group: Japanese additions (Tenmon Kyoto)
figures.story: A mid-level military official in the Imperial Guard divisions, serving as a vital link in the command structure of the capital.

figures.name: Minor Captain
figures.group: Japanese additions (Tenmon Kyoto)
figures.story: A junior officer rank in the Imperial Guard, often held by young nobles as a stepping stone in their political careers.

figures.name: Bureau of Onmyō
figures.native: 陰陽寮(おんみょうりょう)
figures.group: Japanese additions (Tenmon Kyoto)
figures.story: The government department responsible for divination, astronomy, calendar-making, and protection against spiritual misfortunes.

figures.name: Councilor
figures.group: Japanese additions (Tenmon Kyoto)
figures.story: Represents high-ranking advisors who participated in the Council of State to assist the Emperor in national policy.

figures.name: Pacification Command Headquarters
figures.group: Japanese additions (Tenmon Kyoto)
figures.story: Historically referred to regional military commands tasked with the pacification and administration of frontier areas.

figures.name: Director of Market
figures.group: Japanese additions (Tenmon Kyoto)
figures.story: An official in charge of regulating commerce, market prices, and the standard of goods within the capital's designated market areas.

figures.name: Military Inspector
figures.group: Japanese additions (Tenmon Kyoto)
figures.story: An official designated to oversee military readiness and report on the discipline and status of provincial troops.

figures.name: Left Division of Outer Palace Guards
figures.meaning: Left Division of Outer Palace Guards
figures.group: Japanese additions (Tenmon Kyoto)
figures.story: The guard division responsible for the security of the palace, specifically the areas on the left side of the Imperial precinct.

figures.name: Celestial Lake
figures.group: Japanese additions (Tenmon Kyoto)
figures.story: A symbolic heavenly body representing a reservoir or source of water in the sky, vital for the cultivation of the realm.

figures.name: Imperial Bath Matron
figures.group: Japanese additions (Tenmon Kyoto)
figures.story: A high-ranking attendant responsible for the ritual purification and bathing of the infant imperial family members.

figures.name: Imperial Bath Attendant
figures.group: Japanese additions (Tenmon Kyoto)
figures.story: The staff responsible for the physical preparation and assistance during the ritual bathing procedures for the court.

figures.name: Mistress of Staff
figures.group: Japanese additions (Tenmon Kyoto)
figures.story: A female official who acted as a messenger and intermediary between the Emperor and the court, holding significant administrative authority.

figures.name: Court Lady
figures.group: Japanese additions (Tenmon Kyoto)
figures.story: Lower-ranking women in the service of the palace, performing tasks ranging from cleaning to assisting noblewomen.

figures.name: Trout
figures.native: 腹赤(ふくせき・はらか)
figures.group: Japanese additions (Tenmon Kyoto)
figures.story: Named after the river fish, this constellation likely reflects the cultural importance of the imperial food supply and seasonal tributes.

figures.name: Celestial Silkworm
figures.group: Japanese additions (Tenmon Kyoto)
figures.story: Representing the origins of sericulture, a vital industry in ancient Japan that produced the silk worn by the nobility.

figures.name: Right Capital
figures.group: Japanese additions (Tenmon Kyoto)
figures.story: Refers to the western division of the ancient capital (Heian-kyō), an area centered on administration and housing.

figures.name: Left Capital
figures.group: Japanese additions (Tenmon Kyoto)
figures.story: Refers to the eastern division of the ancient capital, which was historically the more prestigious and developed side of the city.

figures.name: Office of Imperial Tombs
figures.group: Japanese additions (Tenmon Kyoto)
figures.story: Responsible for the maintenance, protection, and ritual care of the tombs of past Emperors and noble families.

figures.name: Right Division of Bureau of Horses
figures.meaning: Right Division of Bureau of Horses
figures.group: Japanese additions (Tenmon Kyoto)
figures.story: A government office that managed the imperial stables and horses specifically assigned to the western division.

figures.name: Outer Palace Guard
figures.group: Japanese additions (Tenmon Kyoto)
figures.story: A general term for the military units responsible for maintaining security around the outer boundaries of the imperial palace.

figures.name: Left Division of Bureau of Horses
figures.meaning: Left Division of Bureau of Horses
figures.group: Japanese additions (Tenmon Kyoto)
figures.story: A government office responsible for the management and care of the horses in the eastern division of the imperial palace.

figures.name: Bureau of Accounting
figures.native: 主計(しゅけい・かずえ)
figures.group: Japanese additions (Tenmon Kyoto)
figures.story: An office that audited and managed the state budgets, expenditures, and the overall balance of government finances.

figures.name: Bureau of Military Stores
figures.group: Japanese additions (Tenmon Kyoto)
figures.story: An office responsible for the storage, maintenance, and distribution of military weapons, armor, and equipment.

figures.name: Celestial Rice Bale
figures.group: Japanese additions (Tenmon Kyoto)
figures.story: A symbol of prosperity and the agrarian basis of the nation, representing the collection of rice as tax.

figures.name: Bureau of Taxation
figures.native: 主税(しゅぜい・ちから)
figures.group: Japanese additions (Tenmon Kyoto)
figures.story: Managed the collection of agricultural taxes and handled the administration of national revenue.

figures.name: Bureau of Palace Storehouses
figures.group: Japanese additions (Tenmon Kyoto)
figures.story: Responsible for the management of the palace's dry goods, grains, and other essential supplies required for court life.

figures.name: Pine and Bamboo
figures.group: Japanese additions (Tenmon Kyoto)
figures.story: Plants often used as symbols of longevity and constancy, reflecting the desired stability of the Imperial court.

figures.name: Wild Geese
figures.group: Japanese additions (Tenmon Kyoto)
figures.story: A migratory bird constellation reflecting the changing seasons and the traditional observations of nature by the court.

figures.name: Miscanthus × Giganteus
figures.native: 荻薄(てきはく・オギススキ)
figures.group: Japanese additions (Tenmon Kyoto)
figures.story: A tall grass native to Japan, symbolizing the autumnal landscape and the natural beauty favored by the nobility.

figures.name: Celestial Shaft
figures.group: Japanese additions (Tenmon Kyoto)
figures.story: Represents the structural axle or support, potentially symbolizing the central governance of the state.

figures.name: Dazaifu
figures.group: Japanese additions (Tenmon Kyoto)
figures.story: The administrative center for the Kyushu region, which served as a crucial site for diplomacy with foreign lands.

figures.name: Senior Assistant
figures.group: Japanese additions (Tenmon Kyoto)
figures.story: A high-ranking administrative post within the Dazaifu, responsible for regional policy and border defense.

figures.name: Junior Assistant
figures.group: Japanese additions (Tenmon Kyoto)
figures.story: A subordinate official in the Dazaifu administration who assisted the senior leadership in governing the region.

figures.name: Bureau of Foreign Affairs and Buddhism
figures.meaning: Bureau of Foreign Affairs and Buddhism
figures.group: Japanese additions (Tenmon Kyoto)
figures.story: Handled diplomatic relations with foreign envoys and supervised the affairs of Buddhist temples.

figures.name: Great-grandson
figures.group: Japanese additions (Tenmon Kyoto)
figures.story: A symbolic constellation representing the lineage of the Imperial family and the importance of succession.

figures.name: Great-great-grandson
figures.group: Japanese additions (Tenmon Kyoto)
figures.story: Representing the extended genealogy and the continuity of the imperial bloodline over multiple generations.

figures.name: Open Quiver
figures.group: Japanese additions (Tenmon Kyoto)
figures.story: A traditional military accessory used for carrying arrows, symbolizing the readiness and defensive posture of the state.

figures.name: Closed Quiver
figures.group: Japanese additions (Tenmon Kyoto)
figures.story: A protected case for arrows, representing the disciplined storage and control of military armaments.

figures.name: Hayato (Southern Barbarian Guard)
figures.group: Japanese additions (Tenmon Kyoto)
figures.story: Refers to warriors from southern Japan who were famous for their specialized skills and service in the Imperial palace.

figures.name: Bureau of Higher Education
figures.native: 大学寮(だいがくりょう)
figures.group: Japanese additions (Tenmon Kyoto)
figures.story: The imperial university dedicated to training the sons of the aristocracy in Confucian classics and governance.

figures.name: Bureau of Water Supply
figures.group: Japanese additions (Tenmon Kyoto)
figures.story: Responsible for the management and purification of the water supply used for the Emperor’s consumption and daily needs.

figures.name: Bureau of Textiles
figures.group: Japanese additions (Tenmon Kyoto)
figures.story: An office in charge of the production and weaving of high-quality fabrics and garments for court officials.

figures.name: Bureau of Sake Brewing
figures.group: Japanese additions (Tenmon Kyoto)
figures.story: Managed the production of sake, which was essential for religious ceremonies and official court banquets.

figures.name: Saiku (The Palace of the Saio)
figures.native: 斎宮(さいぐう・いつきのみや)
figures.group: Japanese additions (Tenmon Kyoto)
figures.story: The official residence of the Saio, an Imperial princess who served as a high priestess at the Ise Grand Shrine.

figures.name: Bureau of Court Music
figures.group: Japanese additions (Tenmon Kyoto)
figures.story: Responsible for the performance, training, and preservation of court music and dance, including Gagaku.

figures.name: Right Division of Outer Palace Guards
figures.meaning: Right Division of Outer Palace Guards
figures.group: Japanese additions (Tenmon Kyoto)
figures.story: The guard division tasked with the security of the right side of the imperial palace and its residential quarters.
